sections.h2: What is Morrison County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Morrison County is a mostly rural, river-and-lake county in central Minnesota, and Little Falls anchors it as seat of government and biggest town. Benton County gave up its northern strip to form it on February 25, 1856. The Mississippi River runs south through the western part, and Camp Ripley Military Reservation fills a big piece of the north-central area. Cass, Crow Wing, Mille Lacs, Benton, Stearns and Todd counties surround it.

The QuickFacts table for Morrison County, the July 2025 population estimate is 34,620, with 16,659 housing units across about 1,125 square miles of land. Owners live in 80.6 percent of occupied homes. For 2020 to 2024 the middle owner-occupied home value was $248,500, middle gross rent was $788 a month, and the median household earned $69,446.

The county's school district list includes Little Falls, Pierz, Royalton and Staples-Motley, plus Swanville, Upsala, Holdingford and others. A buyer comparing a house in Little Falls with one near Pierz is also comparing school districts.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for a Morrison County house?
sections.html:
The county's economy is spread thin across small employers. The Census Bureau counted 933 employer establishments and 8,532 jobs there in 2023, and workers spend a mean 28.6 minutes getting to work. About 23.4 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 92 percent of people lived in the same house a year earlier. The county issued 156 building permits in 2025.

Little Falls grew up around water power. A dam and sawmill built there in 1849 supplied the construction of Fort Ripley, and a third dam in 1887 drew in more industry. Pine Tree Lumber Company began its Little Falls operations in 1890, and Hennepin Paper Company started the same year. Charles A. Lindbergh State Park sits inside the county, along with part of Crow Wing State Park.

Sellers can ask the Assessor's Office what classification the parcel carries before listing. The county's appeals page names classification, along with estimated market value, as something an owner may contest.

sections.h2: Which offices in Little Falls deal with property tax and deeds?
sections.html:
All three offices share the Government Center at 213 1st Avenue SE, Little Falls, MN 56345. The county switchboard is 320-632-2941, with a toll-free line at 1-866-401-1111, and the front-line county offices post weekday hours from 8 to 4:30.

  • Auditor/Treasurer: sends the tax bills, collects the money and holds the payment counter. Details are on the county's property tax page.
  • Assessor's Office (Land Services): sets estimated market value and classification, and answers value questions at 320-632-0170.
  • Recorder: files deeds and other real estate papers, phone 320-632-0146. Its web page tells visitors the staff cannot advise on law or draft documents, and refers transfer questions to a real estate attorney or an abstract or title firm.

Online, the county directs people to Beacon for maps and tax statements, and to Landshark for recorded documents.

sections.h2: What are the Morrison County tax payment deadlines?
sections.html:
Two installments make up the real property bill, with deadlines of May 15 and then October 15, and extra dates for resorts, manufactured homes and farmland. Personal property and severed mineral interest taxes fall due alongside the real property installments. The county adds that a deadline falling on a weekend or legal holiday shifts to the next day the office is open.

Due dates on the Morrison County tax payment page
DateWhat is due
May 15Real property, first installment, or the entire bill if it totals $100 or under
May 31Resort property, first half
August 31Manufactured homes, first installment, or the entire bill if it totals $50 or under
October 15Non-agricultural real property, second half
November 15Agricultural real property and manufactured homes, second half

The statewide rule in Minn. Stat. 279.01 uses the same May and October split for bills above $100, and lets agricultural homestead and a few related classes pay the second half through November 15 without penalty.

sections.h2: What payment methods does the Morrison County treasurer accept?
sections.html:
The county lists six channels:

  • Counter: cash or a check made out to Morrison County Auditor/Treasurer, during office hours.
  • Drop box: at Broadway (Highway 27) and 2nd Street SE, emptied every day.
  • Postal mail: addressed to the Auditor/Treasurer at the Government Center. The county treats the postmark as proof of timely mailing.
  • Direct Debit: an enrollment form the county needs 30 days ahead of a due date.
  • Card or eCheck online: American Express, Discover, MasterCard and Visa.
  • Phone: 888-272-9829, then jurisdiction code 3314. Press 1 for personal property, 2 for real estate or 3 for mobile homes.

Fees on electronic payments are 2.59 percent for credit cards, 2.59 percent for debit cards with a $1.10 floor, and $2.15 for an eCheck.

sections.h2: What does a late tax payment cost in Morrison County?
sections.html:
An installment left unpaid at its deadline picks up 2 percent on a homestead and 4 percent on any other property. Section 279.01 repeats that charge when the balance is still open as the next month begins. After that, 1 percent more accrues each month through December. The ceiling is 8 percent for homestead property and 12 percent for everything else.

One break applies to mailed payments. The treasurer has to forgive the penalty if the envelope was postmarked by the Postal Service no more than one business day after the deadline, and only one time per owner. If the postmark is missing or smudged, a signed affidavit from the owner can establish the mailing date. The county board can also let the treasurer waive a penalty that would be unjust and unreasonable, so ask the Auditor/Treasurer whether Morrison County has adopted that policy.

sections.h2: What can you do if your Morrison County valuation looks too high?
sections.html:
Gather evidence and talk to the assessor before any hearing. The county's appeals page says the appeal concerns the current estimated market value or classification, which drives next year's taxes. Its advice is to bring recent comparable sales.

  1. Collect comparable recent sales.
  2. Phone the Assessor's Office at 320-632-0170 and go over your numbers with a county appraiser.
  3. If that fails, book a slot with your local appeal board, which sits in April.
  4. Still unhappy? Book the special appeal board, which sits in June. It will only hear you after the local board has.
  5. The final route is Minnesota Tax Court.

Hearing dates appear on the valuation notice and in local papers. This year's April and June sessions are over, and the next ones follow the same pattern. A dispute over last year's value cannot go to the assessor. It goes to Tax Court only, and must be filed in Tax Court by the end of April of the year the bill comes due.

sections.h2: Does a sale of a Morrison County house change the tax picture?
sections.html:
It does in two ways: the deed has to clear a tax check, and the homestead status resets. Before a deed is accepted for recording, Minn. Stat. 272.12 sends it past the auditor, who searches for unpaid delinquent tax and marks the deed. A recorder cannot take a deed without that mark.

A price above $3,000 also calls for a certificate of value, which section 272.115 has the buyer or seller hand to the auditor. The assessor then takes homestead status off the parcel for the following assessment year, unless the new owner applies and qualifies. With no application on file by December 31, the parcel is treated as nonhomestead that year.

Owing back tax, or holding an inherited or as-is property, is a reason to phone the Auditor/Treasurer for a payoff figure with penalties included. Ask whoever runs your closing how this year's bill will be split.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Morrison County assessor?
faqs.a: The assessor's line is 320-632-0170. For payments and balances, use the Government Center switchboard at 320-632-2941 and ask for the Auditor/Treasurer.

faqs.q: When does the last Morrison County installment fall due?
faqs.a: October 15 closes out non-agricultural real property. Farmland and manufactured homes run to November 15, which is a Sunday this year, so the effective date is Monday, November 16.

faqs.q: Can I use a credit card on my Morrison County tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the county's online payment link or call 888-272-9829 and enter jurisdiction code 3314. Expect a 2.59 percent convenience charge on a credit card.

faqs.q: What is the order of Morrison County appeal steps?
faqs.a: Take it to the assessor first, then the April local board, then the June special board, and finally Minnesota Tax Court. The special board hears only people who already went to the local board.

faqs.q: What does the Census report as a typical home value here?
faqs.a: $248,500, for the 2020 to 2024 period. That middle value covers the entire county, so a given house may differ a lot from that middle point.
